name: Simmons 1983 — The Prisoners' Problem and the Subliminal Channel
notes: Canonical formulation of steganography as a covert channel inside a legitimate one. The 'prisoners' framing is the field's origin problem statement.

name: Anderson & Petitcolas 1998 — On the Limits of Steganography
venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications 16(4)
notes: First-generation survey. Introduces the capacity/robustness/undetectability tradeoff triangle still used to compare techniques.

name: Westfeld & Pfitzmann 1999 — Attacks on Steganographic Systems
notes: Chi-square attack on LSB replacement. The moment the field acknowledged sequential LSB was statistically detectable.

name: Westfeld 2001 — F5: A Steganographic Algorithm
notes: F5: JPEG DCT-coefficient steganography with matrix encoding to reduce embedding rate and shrinkage handling for zero coefficients.

name: Provos 2001 — Defending Against Statistical Steganalysis
notes: OutGuess. JPEG steg that preserves first-order DCT histograms against chi-square-family attacks; introduced statistics-preserving correction pass.

name: Fridrich, Goljan, & Du 2001 — Reliable Detection of LSB Steganography (RS analysis)
notes: RS steganalysis for LSB replacement in grayscale/color images. Estimates embedding rate rather than yes/no; the second pillar of LSB detection alongside chi-square.

name: Dumitrescu, Wu, & Wang 2003 — Detection of LSB Steganography via Sample Pair Analysis
notes: Sample-pair analysis. Same detection class as RS, different statistical assumptions; complementary rather than redundant.

name: Ker 2005 — Weighted Stego Image Steganalysis (WS)
notes: Weighted-stego steganalysis: more accurate than RS/SPA at low embedding rates. Baseline modern LSB detector.

name: Kessler — An Overview of Steganography for the Computer Forensics Examiner
venue: FBI Forensic Science Communications (updated web edition)
notes: Field primer for forensic examiners. Broad rather than deep — good taxonomy reference, less useful for numeric specs.

name: Ange Albertini — Corkami polyglot / abusing file formats catalog
location: https://github.com/corkami/pocs (PoCs and format grammars) + https://github.com/angea/pocorgtfo (PoC||GTFO issue archive)
anchor_artifacts: corkami/pocs/tree/master/mini/polyglots — the minimal polyglot suite (PNG+ZIP, JPEG+ZIP, PDF+ZIP, etc.)
Albertini, 'Abusing file formats', PoC||GTFO 0x07 (2015) — the canonical format-abuse writeup
Albertini, 'Binary art: byte-level construction', PoC||GTFO 0x08 (2015) — PDF+ELF and PDF+other polyglots
notes: Canonical polyglot proof-of-concept catalog. PNG+ZIP, PDF+*, JPEG+*, and the file-format-abuse pattern language used by PoC||GTFO. Not a single paper — a maintained corpus. Cite the specific anchor artifact (mini/polyglots/<name> or PoC||GTFO 0x07 §N) when a claim depends on exact bytes.

name: RFC 2083 — PNG (Portable Network Graphics) Specification
venue: IETF RFC 2083 (1997), superseded by W3C PNG 2nd Edition (2003)
notes: PNG chunk grammar: IHDR/PLTE/IDAT/IEND critical; tEXt/zTXt/iTXt/pHYs/tIME ancillary; ancillary/private/safe-to-copy bits in the chunk-type name. Foundation for chunk-based stego.

name: ITU-T T.81 — JPEG (Digital Compression and Coding of Continuous-Tone Still Images)
notes: Baseline JPEG: DCT block structure (8×8 blocks, quantization tables, zig-zag order), SOI/SOF/DQT/DHT/SOS/EOI markers. F5/jsteg/outguess all target quantized DCT coefficients as defined here.

name: ISO 32000 — Portable Document Format
notes: PDF object model, cross-reference table, incremental updates, embedded streams. Basis for post-EOF, XMP, and incremental-update stego.

name: RFC 3629 — UTF-8, a transformation format of ISO 10646
notes: Definition of UTF-8 byte encoding. Basis for every text stego technique that operates on codepoints (zero-width, homoglyph, VS, combining marks).

name: Unicode UTS #36 — Unicode Security Considerations
notes: Confusables (homoglyphs), IDN homograph attacks, normalization pitfalls. Names the exact codepoints that ST3GG's cyrillic_homoglyph and cjk_homoglyph exploit.

name: Unicode Tag Characters (U+E0000–U+E007F)
venue: Unicode Standard, Tags block (originally UTF-32 language-tag proposal, deprecated for language tagging, repurposed for emoji tag sequences and — accidentally — invisible payloads)
notes: The 'invisible ink' codepoint range. Base for U+E0020–U+E007F ASCII-shadow tag chars and U+E007F cancel-tag. Rendered as nothing in most terminals and web fonts. Foundation of the 2024–2026 LLM prompt-injection stego wave.

name: Unicode Variation Selectors (U+FE00–U+FE0F, U+E0100–U+E01EF)
notes: 256 combining codepoints originally for glyph variants (CJK, emoji presentation VS-15/16). Piggyback on any preceding character; renders as nothing when unrecognized. Basis for ST3GG's `variation` method.

name: Unicode Emoji Tag Sequences (subdivision flags)
notes: Legitimate use of the tag block: black-flag base emoji + ASCII-shadow tag chars + cancel-tag encodes ISO 3166-2 subdivision codes (gbeng, gbsct, gbwls). Every other tag-char payload rides on this same mechanism.

name: Unicode Normalization Forms (UAX #15)
notes: NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD definitions. NFKC canonicalizes cyrillic_homoglyph, cjk_homoglyph, mathbold, fullwidth punctuation, and many combining sequences — the reason those techniques die to aggressive input sanitizers.

name: SNOW — Steganography via Whitespace
notes: Original whitespace-steg tool. Trailing tabs/spaces per line; the reason `slack_paste` kills whitespace steg on the RECODE list.

name: StegDetect / stegbreak
notes: Signature-scan detector for jsteg / jphide / outguess / F5 / invisible-secrets. Referenced by the ST3GG signals field guide as a signature-match hit.

name: zsteg — PNG/BMP steganography detector
notes: Ruby tool. First stop for PNG/BMP LSB CTF work; scans every plausible channel/bit/traversal combination and reports ASCII heads.

name: StegoAppDB — steganography corpus
notes: Reference corpus of stego images produced by 10 mobile stego apps. Basis for benchmarking modern detectors.

name: ALASKA2 — Kaggle Steganalysis Competition (2020)
notes: Kaggle steganalysis competition against JMiPOD/UERD/JUNIWARD. Established modern CNN-based detectors as SOTA against handcrafted schemes.

name: Riley Goodside / Simon Willison — Unicode tag prompt-injection reports
notes: The 2024 wave of Unicode-tag-block prompt injection: hidden instructions that render invisibly but survive many LLM tokenizers. Live threat model for the emoji-tag / invisible-ink techniques.

name: ST3GG v3 header format (this fork)
notes: Password-derived magic bytes (HMAC-SHA256 of a fixed label) plus 16-bit length prefix, optional deflate, optional AES-256-GCM. The extractor gate that requires this header is why raw-bit hides bounce ST3GG's smart_scan.

name: M3GA-ST3GG field guide (persona layer)
notes: The 500-line persona + technique-catalog + heuristic + snippet monolith. Source for most of the initial techniques.json and signatures.json content.

name: M3GA-ST3GG TRANSPORT_MATRIX.md
notes: Human-readable transport-survival matrix. Source for the initial transports.json and survival.json records.

name: M3GA-ST3GG TRANSPORT_RESULTS_SLACK.json
notes: 60-cell empirical result set from a 2026-07-25 Slack probe run. Machine-readable evidence for survival.json Slack rows: pre/post sha256, size deltas, verdict.

name: M3GA-ST3GG README
notes: Repository-level overview. Cited by records that are 'this is how the codebase describes X' rather than 'this is what the primary literature says about X'.
